name: Amaterasu
role: Sun kami and ancestress of the imperial line
fun_fact: Her principal shrine at Ise is rebuilt every twenty years in a ceremony called shikinen sengū.

name: Susanoo
role: Storm kami, brother of the sun, and hero of Izumo
fun_fact: He is credited in the Kojiki with the first recorded Japanese poem, about eight clouds rising over Izumo.

name: Izanagi
role: Creator kami who shaped the islands and fathered the great three
fun_fact: His bath after returning from Yomi is recalled in harae, the Shinto rites of purification.

name: Izanami
role: Creator kami of the islands and ruler of the land of the dead
symbols: the boulder that sealed the pass
fun_fact: The Kojiki says her death came from giving birth to Kagutsuchi, the kami of fire.

name: Tsukuyomi
role: Moon kami and brother of the sun
fun_fact: Few shrines are dedicated to him, and he appears in only a handful of surviving myths.

name: Ōkuninushi
role: Kami of Izumo who helped shape the land and its people
fun_fact: Izumo Taisha is dedicated to him, and in the tenth month the kami are said to gather there.

name: Ninigi-no-Mikoto
role: Heavenly grandchild sent to rule the islands
fun_fact: He is remembered as the great-grandfather of Emperor Jimmu, the legendary first emperor.

name: Kushinada-hime
role: Princess of Izumo saved from the eight-headed serpent
fun_fact: Her name echoes the word kushi, 'comb', and Susanoo hid her as a comb during the serpent's attack.

name: Yamata no Orochi
role: Eight-headed serpent of the Izumo mountains
fun_fact: Its name is often explained as 'eight-forked great serpent', and the Kusanagi sword was found in one of its tails.

name: Sarutahiko Ōkami
role: Kami of the crossroads who guided Ninigi
fun_fact: Travellers and martial artists still honour him, and a shrine near Ise marks the crossroads where he met Ninigi.
